subject: ENGLISH 1
description: ICSE 10th English Language: Voice, Direct & Indirect Speech, Degrees of Comparison, and Synthesis

questions.question: Transform using 'No sooner...': As soon as the bell rang, the children ran out.
options: No sooner the bell rang than the children ran out.
No sooner did the bell ring than the children ran out.
No sooner did the bell ring when the children ran out.
No sooner had the bell rung then the children ran out.
questions.explanation: Correct inversion: 'No sooner did + subject + base verb... than...'

questions.question: Convert to Indirect Speech: The teacher said to Mohan, "Why are you late today?"
options: The teacher asked Mohan that why he was late today.
The teacher asked Mohan why was he late that day.
The teacher asked Mohan why he was late that day.
The teacher inquired Mohan why he is late that day.
questions.explanation: No 'that' after asked with wh-words, word order is assertive (he was late), and 'today' becomes 'that day'.

questions.question: Transform to Comparative Degree: Mount Everest is the highest mountain peak in the world.
options: Mount Everest is higher than any other peak in the world.
Mount Everest is more high than all peaks.
No other peak is higher as Mount Everest.
Very few peaks are higher than Mount Everest.
questions.explanation: Singular superlative -> comparative using 'higher than any other peak in the world'.

questions.question: Transform removing 'too': He is too weak to walk alone.
options: He is so weak that he cannot walk alone.
He is very weak so he can walk alone.
He is too weak so that he cannot walk alone.
He is weak enough that he cannot walk alone.
questions.explanation: 'Too... to' transforms to 'so... that + cannot': 'He is so weak that he cannot walk alone.'

questions.question: Transform into Passive Voice: Who wrote this brilliant novel?
options: Whom was this brilliant novel written?
By whom was this brilliant novel written?
By who this brilliant novel was written?
Who was this brilliant novel written by?
questions.explanation: 'Who' changes to 'By whom' followed by auxiliary verb and subject: 'By whom was this brilliant novel written?'
